title: Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity equals the Koszul Euler characteristic

standard_prerequisites.use: Noetherian local algebra, Hilbert–Samuel polynomial, Artin–Rees, filtered-complex spectral sequences, length additivity, and the elementary finite-difference identity. None states the Koszul multiplicity equality.

core_obligations: Build the degree-shifted I-adic filtration on the Koszul complex and identify its associated graded differential.
Prove finite-length control and Artin–Rees convergence, then convert the spectral-sequence Euler sum into the Hilbert–Samuel finite difference.

proof_roadmap.step: Build the degree-shifted I-adic filtration on the Koszul complex and identify its associated graded differential.
Prove finite-length control and Artin–Rees convergence, then convert the spectral-sequence Euler sum into the Hilbert–Samuel finite difference.

difficulty_reason: Even after standard spectral sequence and Artin–Rees tools, the filtration must simultaneously encode the Koszul differential and Hilbert–Samuel degree. The finite-length and convergence argument connecting these invariants is a substantial H2 commutative-algebra proof.

editorial_notes: The historical review incorrectly paraphrases equality of Euler sums as E_infinity=E_1. The source 1064–1069 only equates alternating length sums; no degeneration at E_1 is assumed.
The finite-difference identity is ordinary polynomial algebra and is an allowed prerequisite; it is not another counted problem.
